Sara — thanks, this is helpful context. TL;DR: we can support a staged 12+12 with a single private offer activation if structured as a 12-mo initial commitment with a written amendment (preferred), otherwise two separate offers are required and each will hit the buyer approval flow independently. Details below.

Option A — Single private offer + amendment (recommended) - Redwood publishes a 12-month private offer on AWS Marketplace at the co-sell price. - After signature we activate the offer and the customer receives co-sell entitlements immediately (single activation). - For the 2nd year we execute an amendment to the original PO (DocuSign addendum referencing the original deal id) — this avoids a second Marketplace seller-led approval and keeps co-sell pricing consistent.

Tradeoffs: requires legal to accept an amendment approach; activation velocity is fast for year 1 and year 2 is procedural.

Option B — Two sequential private offers (12mo + 12mo) - Each offer needs its own buyer approval flow and potentially new co-sell window evaluation. - Slower (approval latency can stack) but sometimes simpler for finance teams that want separate purchase orders.

Operational notes - If Acme's procurement can sign an amendment form (we can provide a template), we estimate activation-in-marketplace within 2 business days after DocuSign completes for year 1. - If two offers are needed, expect ~3–6 weeks for the second offer's buyer approval depending on buyer org routing.

Next steps
1) Do you want Redwood to share an amendment template we use for 12+12 deals?
2) If legal prefers two offers, we can prepare the second offer but recommend lining up approvers in parallel to compress latency.

Attaching a quick pricing scenario spreadsheet (unit rates for 12 vs 24 and amendment pricing). Happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement + finance this week.

Cheers,
